relationships.subject: Parkinson's disease
relationships.evidence_quote: We found higher expression of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-2 (p<0.001) and TNF-α (p<0.01) in skin samples of patients with PD compared to healthy controls

relationships.subject: Parkinson's disease
relationships.evidence_quote: we observed a higher expression of IL-1β in the skin of patients in the PD Pain group compared to healthy controls (p<0.05)

relationships.subject: IL-1beta
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, IL-1β stimulates the expression of cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 [44]

relationships.subject: alpha-synuclein
relationships.evidence_quote: α-synuclein is known to trigger the expression of proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β in vitro [46]

key_findings: Skin of PD patients showed lower IENFD and higher IL-2 and TNF-alpha expression regardless of pain; IL-1beta was higher only in PD with pain versus controls.
The data do not support local skin inflammation as a driver of pain in PD.
